result:
Confirmed re-runs are idempotent (the fixture cleanup at the top of `beforeAll` handles that) and stable.

## Summary

The root cause was `routes/web.ts:35` — `posts.get('/archive/:date*', ...)`. In this Hono-based router, `:date*` is not a multi-segment wildcard; `*` is just a legal character in a param name, so it registers a single path segment whose param key is literally `"date*"`, not `"date"`. That explains all three symptoms: `/posts/archive/2026/08` 404s because the route pattern only has one segment after `archive` and can't match a two-segment path; `/posts/archive/2026` 422s because it does match, but `ArchiveParamSchema` looks for a `date` key while the actual param is keyed `date*`, so Zod sees it as missing; and the leading-zero variant never got the chance to matter since the route itself never matched two-segment paths.

The fix changes the route to `posts.get('/archive/:date{.+}', ...)`, Hono's documented syntax for a regex-constrained param that can span multiple path segments (including the `/`), which correctly names the param `date` and captures `"2026"` or `"2026/08"` as before intended — no changes needed to the controller or `ArchiveParamSchema`. I regenerated the route codegen (`bun run codegen`) so `.guren/routes.gen.ts` and `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` reflect the new pattern, and added a `posts.archive` test suite to `tests/PostController.test.ts` covering month lookup (zero-padded and not), year lookup, year/month cross-contamination, empty periods, and out-of-range months. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (8/8).
